fi-valenciennea-puellaris.title: Diamond Watchman Goby
fi-valenciennea-puellaris.summary: A sand-sifting goby that keeps the sand bed stirred and clean.
rows: About 6 in; wild record 20 cm (7.9 in) SL (standard length) (FishBase)
Fights with its own kind unless a mated pair
Carnivore. Sifts sand for small animals; supplement with live and frozen meaty foods
Indo-Pacific: Red Sea to Samoa, north to southern Japan, south to the Great Barrier Reef and New Caledonia
notes: Needs a sand bed and does best with a refugium supplying natural food.

fi-amblyeleotris-yanoi.title: Flagtail Shrimp Goby
fi-amblyeleotris-yanoi.summary: A brightly marked shrimp goby that can share a burrow with a pistol shrimp.
rows: About 5 in; wild record 13 cm (5.1 in) SL (standard length) (FishBase)
Western Pacific: Ryukyu Islands to Papua New Guinea
notes: Pairs with alpheid (pistol) shrimp; give it a sand bed for a burrow.

fi-tigrigobius-multifasciatus.title: Greenbanded Goby
fi-tigrigobius-multifasciatus.summary: A tiny green-and-dark banded goby for small reef or fish-only tanks.
rows: About 2 in; wild record 5 cm (2 in) TL (FishBase)
Can be kept in small groups of three or more
Carnivore. Live and frozen brine and mysis shrimp and other carnivore foods
Western Atlantic: Bahamas and Central America to northern South America

fi-stonogobiops-nematodes.title: High-Fin Banded Goby
fi-stonogobiops-nematodes.summary: A small banded shrimp goby (also called the Blackray Shrimp Goby) that can pair with a pistol shrimp.
rows: About 2 in; wild record 6 cm (2.4 in) SL (standard length) (FishBase)
Indo-West Pacific: Seychelles, the Philippines, and Bali, Indonesia
notes: Can live in tanks as small as about 10 gal with live rock and sand.
Not aggressive toward other shrimp gobies.

fi-valenciennea-sexguttata.title: Six Spot Sleeper Goby
fi-valenciennea-sexguttata.summary: A white sand-sifting goby with blue spots on the cheeks.
rows: About 5½ in; wild record 14 cm (5.5 in) TL (FishBase)
Carnivore. Sifts sand for food; supplement with frozen meaty foods
Indo-Pacific: Red Sea, Persian Gulf and East Africa to Samoa; north to Yaeyama Islands, Ryukyu Islands, south to Queensland, Australia
notes: Needs a live sand bed, ideally with a refugium supplying natural food.

fi-valenciennea-wardii.title: Tiger Watchman Goby
rows: About 5 in; wild record 15 cm (5.9 in) SL (standard length) (FishBase)
Fights with its own kind unless a male-female pair
Carnivore. Sifts the sand bed; offer live and frozen brine and mysis shrimp
Indo-Pacific: extremely rare, known from widely scattered localities in the Indian Ocean and western tropical Pacific
notes: Needs a live sand bed, ideally with a refugium.

fi-cryptocentrus-cinctus.title: Yellow Watchman Goby
fi-cryptocentrus-cinctus.summary: A classic burrowing goby that often pairs with a pistol (snapping) shrimp.
rows: About 4 in; wild record 10 cm (3.9 in) SL (standard length) (FishBase)
Fights with its own kind unless a mated pair
Western Pacific: Yaeyama Islands, Japan to Singapore and the southern Great Barrier Reef; Palau and Truk in Micronesia
notes: Wants a sand bottom with loose rubble for burrowing.
warn: May jump; use a tight-fitting lid.

fi-valenciennea-strigata.title: Gold Head Sleeper Goby
fi-valenciennea-strigata.summary: A sand-sifting goby with a yellow head and a blue streak on the face. It keeps the sand bed turned over.
rows: About 6 in; wild record 18 cm (7.1 in) TL (FishBase)
Fights with its own kind unless a mated pair
Carnivore. Sifts mouthfuls of sand for food; also live and frozen brine shrimp, mysis and carnivore foods, fed often
Indo-Pacific: East Africa to Tuamoto Islands, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to Sydney, Australia, including Lord Howe Island
notes: Needs a live sand bed and, ideally, a refugium.

fi-nemateleotris-magnifica.title: Firefish (Fire Goby)
fi-nemateleotris-magnifica.summary: A slender dartfish with a yellow head, white body and red tail, always flicking its tall front dorsal fin. It hovers above the rock and darts into a hole when startled.
rows: About 3 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 9 cm (3.5 in) TL (FishBase)
Carnivore. Foods: mysis shrimp, enriched brine shrimp, plankton, finely chopped seafood, small marine pellets, marine flakes
Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Hawaiian, Marquesan and Pitcairn islands, north to the Ryukyu Islands
notes: A known jumper: keep the tank covered.
Adults are usually kept singly or as a pair.

fi-pholidichthys-leucotaenia.title: Engineer Goby (Convict Blenny)
fi-pholidichthys-leucotaenia.summary: Neither a goby nor a blenny: an eel-like fish from the Philippines to the Solomon Islands. Juveniles are striped and school; adults dig tunnels under the rockwork.
rows: About 13.4 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 34 cm (13.4 in) TL (FishBase)
Carnivore. Foods: mysis shrimp, enriched brine shrimp, krill, chopped fresh or frozen seafood, meaty carnivore pellets, live artemia
Western Central Pacific: Philippines south to the Solomon Islands
notes: It moves a lot of sand: set the main rockwork on the tank bottom, not on the sand, so tunnelling cannot topple it.
Anything mouth-sized, including small shrimp and crabs, may be eaten.

fi-nemateleotris-decora.title: Purple Firefish (Decorated Firefish)
fi-nemateleotris-decora.summary: A slim dartfish with a lavender body, a purple face and dark red-purple fins, from deeper Indo-Pacific reef slopes. Peaceful, hardy and reef safe.
rows: About 4 in (Saltwaterfish.com adult size); wild record 9 cm (3.5 in) TL (FishBase)
Often found in pairs in the wild
Carnivore/planktivore: frozen or live mysis and enriched brine shrimp
Indo-Pacific: Mauritius to Samoa, north to Ryukyu Islands, south to New Caledonia
notes: May squabble with other gobies, blennies or dartfish in small tanks.
warn: A known jumper: keep a tight-fitting lid.

fi-amblyeleotris-diagonalis.title: Diagonal Shrimp Goby
fi-amblyeleotris-diagonalis.summary: A sand-dwelling goby with diagonal bands that shares a burrow with a pistol shrimp in the wild. Hardy and reef safe, but territorial toward other gobies.
rows: Territorial and aggressive toward similar fish
Small meaty foods: mysis, brine shrimp and similar, fed several times a day
Indo-Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa to the Solomons and Great Barrier Reef
notes: Keep the tank covered: it is known to jump.
Best with an Alpheus pistol shrimp partner and a sandy, rubbly bottom it can dig in.
